title: Seekh Kebab

ingredients.title: For the Kebabs
items: Minced lamb or beef – 1 kg, finely ground, ideally 20% fat
Red onions – 2 medium, finely grated and moisture squeezed out
Fresh coriander leaves – 1 cup, finely chopped
Fresh mint leaves – ½ cup, finely chopped
Garam masala powder – 2 tsp, freshly ground preferred
Black pepper – ½ tsp, freshly ground
Melted ghee or mustard oil – 2 tbsp

instruction.title: Prepare the Meat Mixture
steps: Place the finely minced meat in a large chilled mixing bowl.
Add grated onion, making sure it has been squeezed thoroughly to remove excess moisture.
Add ginger paste, garlic paste, green chilies, coriander leaves, and mint leaves.
Add roasted cumin powder, garam masala, ground coriander, Kashmiri red chili powder, black pepper, chaat masala, and salt.
Add the lightly roasted gram flour and melted ghee or mustard oil.
Mix thoroughly with your hands for 8–10 minutes until the mixture becomes sticky and cohesive.

instruction.title: Rest the Mixture
steps: Cover the meat mixture and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
For deeper flavor and easier shaping, refrigerate overnight.
Keep the mixture chilled until ready to shape.

instruction.title: Shape the Kebabs
steps: Lightly oil your hands and the skewers.
Take a portion of the chilled meat mixture and place it around a skewer.
Press and mold the mixture gently around the skewer to form a long cylinder about 6–8 inches long.
Make sure the kebabs are evenly thick so they cook uniformly.
Repeat with the remaining mixture.

instruction.title: Cook – Tandoor or Grill
steps: Preheat the tandoor or grill to high heat.
Place the skewered kebabs directly over the heat.
Cook for about 8–10 minutes, rotating regularly.
Continue cooking until the kebabs are cooked through and evenly charred on the outside.

instruction.title: Cook – Oven Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 240°C / 475°F.
Place the kebabs on a greased rack positioned over a baking tray.
Cook for 12–15 minutes, turning halfway through.
Finish under the broiler for 2–3 minutes to develop a lightly charred exterior.

instruction.title: Optional Dhungar Smoky Finish
steps: Heat a small piece of charcoal until it becomes red-hot.
Place the hot charcoal in a small heatproof steel bowl inside the kebab tray.
Pour 1 tsp ghee over the charcoal.
Immediately cover the tray with a lid and let the smoke infuse for about 2 minutes.
Remove the charcoal and serve the kebabs immediately.

instruction.title: Serve
steps: Transfer the hot seekh kebabs to a serving platter.
Garnish with a light sprinkle of chaat masala.
Serve with mint-coriander chutney, sliced onions, lemon wedges, and butter naan.

chefTips: Meat: Use minced meat with around 20% fat for juicy, tender kebabs.
Moisture control: Squeeze the grated onion thoroughly; excess moisture can cause the mixture to fall apart.
Binding: Mix the meat vigorously for 8–10 minutes until sticky and cohesive for better skewer binding.
Temperature: Keep the meat mixture cold while shaping; warm meat is more likely to break apart on the skewers.
Cooking: High heat creates the characteristic smoky, charred exterior while keeping the center juicy.
Chicken variation: If using lean chicken mince, add 1 tbsp cream and an additional 1 tbsp besan to improve moisture and binding.
